learning_outcomes.text: Provide students with a solid foundation in solving electrical networks.
Understand the operation of basic components: sources, resistors, capacitors, coils.
Provide students with a solid foundation in networks with semiconductor components: transistors and simple OPAMPs.
Understand the structure and operation of transistors: BJT and FET.
Analyze and design circuits containing transistors.
Practice solving and analyzing the above aspects.
Build, measure, and design the above circuits with semiconductors.
Encourage students to use computer simulations and the internet.
Enable students to make connections between simulations, calculations, and measurements.
Promote self-reliance by teaching a specific study and working method.
Allow students to practice solving and analyzing networks with semiconductor components (transistors and FET's).
Teach students to design, build and measure the above circuits.
Teach students to make circuits error-free.
Let students use computer simulations and the internet.
Let students make connections between simulations, calculations, and measurements.
Promote self-reliance by teaching a specific study and working method.

syllabus_topics: Structure and operation of Bipolar Junction Transistor (BJT)
Analysis and design of important circuits with BJT
Structure and operation of Field Effect Transistor (FET)
Analysis and design of important circuits with FET
Basic concepts and operation of thyristor, diac, triac, and IGBT
Structure and operation of Bipolar Junction Transistor (BJT)
Analysis and design of important transistor circuits
Structure and operation of Field Effect Transistor (FET)
teaching_methods: Promoting self-reliance through a specific study and work method
Promoting/stimulating the use of computer simulations and the internet
Making connections between simulations, calculations, and measurements

assessment_methods.method: Oral exam with prior preparation of a workpiece (Lab)

assessment_rules: For the Analog electronics theory, there is an oral exam with written preparation in the second exam period (June), counting for 100%. For the Analog electronics lab, the second exam opportunity in the third exam period (August) is an oral exam (100%) with prior preparation of a workpiece. After deliberation, an assignment is given to the student, and the practical execution and results are brought to the exam for demonstration and explanation. Partial transfers are possible for successful partial results (YT5297 - Electronics - advanced: theory + exercise and YT5373 - Electronics - advanced: lab) within the academic year.
bibliography: Electronic principles, Albert Malvino, David J. Bates, ISBN-10: 0-07-110699-5
